dump.name: gtfo-inspection/dumper/dump.cs
dump.note: Local read-only copy used for this audit. dump.cs records the short type name, the il2cpp RVA and the exact parameter list.

used.name: Modules-ASM.dll
used.readWith: Mono.Cecil metadata reading (member kinds and enum constants only)

used.name: UnityEngine.CoreModule.dll
used.readWith: Mono.Cecil metadata reading; `Transform` and `GameObject` live in this assembly, not in Modules-ASM

question: Where can authored gear-part poses be applied so that every locally visible copy of a gear is posed, and exactly which native members does that require writing?

answer.hook: Gear.GearPartHolder.OnAllPartsSpawned, postfix, HarmonyPriority.Last. The body runs once per holder after every part of that holder exists, so it is the only point at which no part is still missing.
answer.writeSet: Exactly four presentation members: UnityEngine.Transform::set_localPosition, UnityEngine.Transform::set_localEulerAngles, UnityEngine.Transform::set_localScale and UnityEngine.GameObject::SetActive. Every value is absolute, so re-running the body cannot accumulate.
answer.readSet: The gear's own offline block record (Gear.GearPartHolder::get_GearIDRange -> Gear.GearIDRange::get_PlayfabItemInstanceId, the same record the gear-block mount reads), the per-component readback Gear.GearIDRange::GetCompID(Gear.eGearComponent), the twenty-one part objects Gear.GearPartHolder exposes, and UnityEngine.Transform::Find for a child path.
answer.network: None. The hook publishes no fact, joins no command and touches no game state; every machine that has the same package reads its own files and poses its own holders, so consistency comes from the package, not from a message.

hook.name: OnAllPartsSpawned

methodPointerTable.meaning: The il2cpp method-pointer table in `.data` holds this method's address, which is how the holder reaches it without a literal E8 call site.

sameNameSibling.meaning: A different type declares a method of the same name, so the patch has to name the type as well as the method. `native.hook.GearPartsSpawned.unique-game-method` in tests/NativeLayout is what keeps the two apart: the patch declaration must resolve to exactly one game method.

hook.callGraphLimit: OnAllPartsSpawned has no literal E8 caller in this image; its address appears only in the method-pointer table. The body's own prologue is verified at its RVA, and a spawned holder necessarily reaches it (GearPartCustomization has patched this exact member in shipped use), but the dispatch site itself is not decoded here.
hook.multiplicity: One holder = one body run. First-person gear, another player's third-person copy, the menu preview (CM_PageGearDetails), an icon render (GearIconRendering) and a deployed sentry (SentryGunInstance : ItemEquippable) each build their own holder through GearBuilder/GearManager, so each reaches this body on its own machine. Nothing in the body distinguishes them, which is why one authored file poses every view.

readSet.note: Readers only; the layout suite pins this list exactly, so a new native read fails the build until it is reviewed here.
readSet.blockId: The block id comes from the record the game's own offline gear loader writes (evidence/w5-gear-block.json); the applier calls EquipmentNativeAdapter.GearBlockId, the same function the gear-block mount matcher answers from, so one spelling of a block id exists in the package.
readSet.partId: Gear.GearIDRange::GetCompID(Gear.eGearComponent) is the game's own per-component readback. An authored `partId` is compared against it; a slot whose block differs (or reads back 0, which is no block) keeps the game's pose.

writeSet.note: This is the whole presentation-write whitelist. `native.read-only-game-access` in tests/NativeLayout fails on any other non-getter game member, and `native.presentation-writes-exact` fails if one of these four stops being used.

members.meaning: Absolute local position in metres, per axis within 1 m (the loader refuses more).
Absolute local euler angles in degrees, normalized into [0, 360) by the loader so one pose has one authored spelling.
Absolute local scale multiplier, per axis within [0.05, 4].
Whether the part is shown. This build's interop exposes no `active` property, so `SetActive` is the only spelling of the ruling's `GameObject.active`.

notWritten: No DataBlock, no ArchetypeDataBlock and no GearIDRange field: the online/offline gear data is untouched.
No network call and no command: the write set is local presentation only.
An omitted field in a file is never written at all, so the game's own pose survives for everything the author did not name.

slots.note: A pose names an `eGearComponent` member; the production enum `GearPartSlot` carries the build's own number for it, checked member by member against Modules-ASM by `native.gear-part-slots-exact`.
slots.excluded: The other `eGearComponent` members (perks, types, MuzzleFlash, ShellCasing, Pattern, Palette, DecalA/B and so on) have no `GameObject` field on `GearPartHolder`, so a file cannot name them and a file that does is refused whole.
slots.fieldOffsets: dump.cs records the twenty-one fields at 0x28..0xC8 in the order above; nothing in the package reads or writes by offset.

dataFile.nameRule: The file name is the canonical decimal block id and the file's own `blockId` text has to be the same digits; both spellings are the catalog's. One block is defined by one file: when two or more files claim the same block, the block is withdrawn whole (no file wins by ordinal scan order) and every claiming file is named once.
dataFile.shape: { blockId, parts: [ { component, partId?, enabled?, localPosition?, localEulerAngles?, localScale?, children: [ { path, ...same fields, children? } ] } ] }. A child entry may nest `children` of its own, and the whole tree is applied: every node carries its full path from the part, which is what is handed to the game's own hierarchy lookup, and a node that is not there takes its subtree with it (one line for the highest missing node of a branch).

limits.childPathCounting: Counted on the finished path from the part, a nested node's own segments plus every segment above it, so nesting cannot pass the cap one level at a time; each segment must be non-empty and neither `.` nor `..`.

dataFile.loading: Read once at plugin start into an immutable snapshot; a bad file is refused on its own with one error line naming the file and the first reason, and the other files still load. A block claimed by two or more files is not loaded at all, so a pose never depends on which file the scan reached first.

hostOff.behaviour: Plugin.Load returns before any registration or native work when the host is configured Off, so with `ForgeRuntime` Off this package neither reads the authored files nor installs the hook: no gear part is posed at all, on any machine.
hostOff.achieved: The package keeps working with the files that are there and has no separate Off mode of its own; turning the host off is what disables it, which is the same shape every other native hook in this package has.

limits: No claim about runtime behaviour: nothing here was executed. The hook's dispatch site is not decoded (see callGraphLimit); a direct method-pointer entry is evidence that the body is reachable, not that this body ran in a game.

Whether an animator overwrites the written local pose after the holder spawns is not answered here: `GearPartHolder::Update` exists (dump.cs line 614843) and its body was not decoded. It is listed as a game-side confirmation item.
The scale band and the 1 m position cap are authored limits from the ruling, not native ones: the game accepts any finite value.
A holder assembled before the plugin loads, or one the game rebuilds without running this body, keeps the game's pose.
